Shoryamishra61 opened PR #14947 from Shoryamishra61:fix/interrupt-poll-14926 to bytecodealliance:main:

Fixes #14926

Why this change is needed

When inlining functions that contain interrupt_poll or compiling functions where an interrupt_poll possesses user stack maps, Cranelift encountered several issues:

  1. Inliner Crash / Unknown Call Opcode: interrupt_poll has Opcode::is_call() == true because it transfers control to the runtime interpreter, but it lacks a FuncRef / external callee body. The inliner previously hit the unhandled call assertion.
  2. Calling Convention Invariant: The IR verifier mandates that interrupt_poll only appears in functions with the tail calling convention. Inlining a tail callee containing an interrupt_poll into a caller with a different convention (e.g. system_v) resulted in invalid CLIF.
  3. Exception Table Fixups: When inlining into a try_call site, exception table fixups attempted to inspect interrupt_poll as a callable target.
  4. Backend Safepoints & Stack Map PC: Neither the x64 nor AArch64 backends classified InterruptPoll as a safepoint (is_safepoint()), and stack maps were not attached to the faulting load instruction PC where runtime signal handlers inspect frame state.
  5. Consecutive Stack Map PC Collision: In rare cases where a preserve_all call immediately precedes an interrupt_poll and both have stack maps, the call return PC and the faulting load PC coincide, violating exact-PC stack map uniqueness.

Implementation Highlights

  • Inliner (cranelift/codegen/src/inline.rs):
    • Allowed interrupt_poll to pass through the instruction-copying loop without tripping the unhandled call assertion.
    • Added can_inline check requiring callers to have CallConv::Tail if the callee contains interrupt_poll; non-tail callers preserve the out-of-line call.
    • Restricted exception table fixup candidates to Call, CallIndirect, TryCall, and TryCallIndirect.
  • ISA Backends (cranelift/codegen/src/isa/{x64, aarch64}/inst/):
    • Updated is_safepoint() to return true for Inst::InterruptPoll.
    • Emitted user stack maps at the address of the faulting load (sink.cur_offset()).
    • Emitted an architecture-specific NOP (x64: 0x90, AArch64: 0xd503201f) when a preceding call stack map shares the same PC with the poll's stack map.
  • MachBuffer & Disassembly (buffer.rs, write.rs):
    • Added MachBuffer::last_user_stack_map_pc() to detect PC collisions.
    • Generalized write.rs to print user stack maps for any safepoint instruction in textual CLIF output.
  • Regression Tests (cranelift/filetests/):
    • Added 5 new CLIF fixtures covering inliner behavior, x64/AArch64 stack map emission, and consecutive call/poll PC collision handling.

Verification Done

The following test suites were executed locally against current upstream main (257ecb40e665):

  • issue_repro_1.clif and issue_repro_2.clif from #14926 (PASSED)
  • cargo run -p cranelift-tools -- test cranelift/filetests/filetests (1,387 tests PASSED)
  • cargo test -p cranelift-codegen -j 1 (204 unit tests, 22 doctests PASSED)
  • cargo test -p cranelift-filetests -j 1 (3 unit tests, 1 doctest PASSED)
  • cargo fmt -p cranelift-codegen -- --check & cargo clippy -p cranelift-codegen --all-targets -- -D warnings (PASSED, 0 warnings)
  • cargo run --release -p cranelift-tools -j 1 -- test <5 fixtures> (release build compiled and 5 regression tests PASSED)

AI Tool Usage Disclosure

In compliance with the Bytecode Alliance AI Tool Use Policy: An AI assistant (Antigravity) was used locally to assist with forward-porting the patch to current upstream main, running test harness commands, resolving trailing whitespace on test fixtures, and formatting this submission text. All code logic, test results, and diffs were inspected and reviewed.
Shoryamishra61 removed the review request for wasmtime-compiler-reviewers from PR #14947.
:memo: alexcrichton submitted PR review.

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

It's ok to trim down verbose LLM comments like this. Basically this just needs to convey "InterruptPoll returns is_call(), but it doesn't participate in inlining"

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

IIRC we've already got inlining heuristics elsewhere in Wasmtime which would cover things like this. Subjectively I'd say it's ok to drop this and leave this up to callers, and if the heuristics from Wasmtime are ever extracted we could perhaps consolidate with this.

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

IIRC we've already got infrastructure in other places for whether or not metadata applies to after an instruction or that instruction itself (or something like that). For example I think MachDebugTagPos serves that purpose. Personally I think it would be better to improve stack map lookup to handle that as opposed to injecting otherwise-not-useful nops.

cfallin commented on PR #14947:

interrupt_poll has Opcode::is_call() == true

My intuition here is that this is probably the wrong decision, in hindsight: yes it can "do a call" in a sense, if a signal handler runs, but that's completely transparent. The "can call" opcode characteristic is really more relevant for things like inlining, as we see here, and in most ways the opcode is not a call (with args, with a callee, etc). So we should probably flip the condition here and then work through the implications, IMHO.

(I will take a more detailed look next week when I am fully back at the keyboard; I just wanted to leave this thought now as the discussion is open)
